title: Rosh Hashanah: kingship, memory, shofar
hook: the extra service has three parts: God as king, God remembering, the shofar

segments.voice: Yesterday, the world's birthday. Your line was happy birthday, world. Today, the heart of the Rosh Hashanah service, in three parts.

On most Shabbats and festivals, the additional Amidah, the Musaf, has seven blessings. On Rosh Hashanah it has nine. The three in the middle are each built like a small anthology: ten verses chosen from across the Bible, stitched into a prayer, and followed, in many synagogues, by the shofar. Ever sat through a Rosh Hashanah service and wondered why it's so long? This is a big part of the answer.
screen: `SEVEN BLESSINGS BECOME NINE.` → `TEN VERSES EACH.` → `WHY IT'S SO LONG.`

segments.voice: The three middle blessings are Malchuyot, kingship; Zichronot, remembrances; and Shofarot, the shofar. The Talmud, in Rosh Hashanah 16a, explains them as if God were speaking: say before Me kingships, so that you make Me king over you; remembrances, so that your memory rises before Me for good. And how? With the shofar. The Mishnah asks for ten verses for each. In the prayer book they're drawn from the Torah, the Writings and the Prophets, ending with the Torah again. One Malchuyot verse comes from the Song of the Sea: "The LORD shall reign for ever and ever." The prayer that opens Malchuyot is Aleinu, our duty to praise, the one that ends every daily service. Tradition says it began here, as the introduction to kingship on Rosh Hashanah, and only later moved into the everyday. On Rosh Hashanah, at the words we bend the knee, many congregations don't just bow. They kneel, and bow to the floor. Why start the new year with kingship? In the old world, a king was the one whose word ruled your days. To say God is king is to ask: what actually rules my life? My phone. My fear. My boss. The approval of people I don't even like. Malchuyot is a yearly audit of loyalties. Before the tradition asks God to remember you, it asks you to decide whom you serve.
screen: `KINGSHIP, MEMORY, SHOFAR.` · `MAKE ME KING OVER YOU.` · `TEN VERSES, THREE KINDS OF BOOK.` · `ALEINU BEGAN HERE.` · then, large: `WHO IS KING?`

segments.voice: Be honest about what actually sets your schedule, your mood and your choices, and name two or three things without judging them; some may be good, a child, a calling, and some may not. Then ask what you'd want to rule your days if you could choose. If you pray, you can say the line from the Song of the Sea, the LORD shall reign; if not, name the value you'd crown.
Malchuyot. Kingships. The first of the three great middle blessings of the Rosh Hashanah Musaf, where God is declared king.
Your line: who is king. Kingship first, then memory, and only then the shofar. Until tomorrow.

notes: Rosh Hashanah 16a / 34b: 'say before Me kingships... remembrances... and with what? with the shofar'; confirm.
Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:6: no fewer than ten verses each; the order Torah, Writings, Prophets, closing with Torah follows Talmudic practice; confirm.
Shofar after each of the three blessings is Ashkenazi/Sephardi standard practice; some sound during the silent Amidah too.
Exodus 15:18 is among the Malchuyot verses in standard machzorim; confirm.
